tools.name: list_micro_markets
tools.description: List the markets this marketplace facilitates (asset, chain, currencies, fee).

tools.name: get_listings
tools.description: Active listings/auctions for a market. Each row carries the ask and the position's underlying contents priced at current market (published formula: /docs#data-sources), plus discountPct (the difference between them). Sorted by discount percentage, descending.

tools.name: get_listing_details
tools.description: Full detail for one order including a FRESH live-contents snapshot (principal, claimable rewards, voting/earning power, as_of_block).

tools.name: get_recent_trades
tools.description: Recently settled sales for a market. `amount` is the EXACT settled total (incl. fee) from the on-chain fill where the indexer recorded it, with `settledAt` the block time and `exact: true`; otherwise it falls back to the listed ask with `exact: false` (a decayed Dutch auction settles BELOW its liste

tools.name: prepare_purchase
tools.description: Prepare the non-custodial transaction package to BUY a listing (or accept an offer): ordered approvals + Seaport fulfillOrder calldata + a fresh contents snapshot. prepared.summary quotes the CURRENT price (Dutch auctions interpolate, asOf says when); the approval grants approveBaseUnits — slightly

tools.name: prepare_offer
tools.description: Prepare a BID/offer on a position: returns the Seaport order to sign (EIP-712), the currency approval needed, and how to submit it. The agent reads its Seaport counter, signs, and POSTs the signed order — settlement stays on Seaport.

tools.name: prepare_listing
tools.description: Prepare a SELL listing or Dutch auction. Verifies the seller OWNS the position and it's transferable (not voted/attached), builds the Seaport order with the Interface fee injected by the server, and returns the one-time NFT approval + EIP-712 typed data to sign. Never signs or holds keys.

tools.name: prepare_cancel
tools.description: Prepare the on-chain Seaport cancel transaction for an active order. Only the order's offerer can execute it (Seaport enforces msg.sender == offerer), so the calldata is safe to return. After it confirms, POST { txHash } to the confirm endpoint to update the book.

tools.name: get_orders
tools.description: List orders created by an address (its listings, auctions, offers). Status is reconciled by the background worker — treat as advisory until checked at fill.

tools.name: get_owned_positions
tools.description: List the positions an address owns in a market, with listability (voted/attached positions can't transfer).

tools.name: subscribe_notifications
tools.description: Subscribe a wallet to push notifications (order_filled / offer_received / saved_search) via an HMAC-signed webhook — the agent-native alternative to polling. tools.name: list_subscriptions
tools.description: List a wallet's notification subscriptions (webhook URLs redacted to origin).

tools.name: unsubscribe_notifications
tools.description: Delete a notification subscription. Two-step like subscribe_notifications: call without `signature` to get the message to sign. `chainId` is signed over and verified on that chain. Signed messages are single-use.

findings.detail: Description of "subscribe_notifications" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: subscribe_notifications, list_subscriptions, unsubscribe_notifications · Private data: prepare_purchase, subscribe_notifications, list_subscriptions · Public sink: prepare_purchase, prepare_offer, prepare_cancel, subscribe_notifications, list_subscriptions · Destructive: prepare_cancel, unsubscribe_notifications.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: subscribe_notifications, list_subscriptions, unsubscribe_notifications · Private data: prepare_purchase, subscribe_notifications, list_subscriptions · Public sink: prepare_purchase, prepare_offer, prepare_cancel, subscribe_notifications, list_subscriptions · Destructive: prepare_cancel, unsubscribe_notifications

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "prepare_offer" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

Name markets (basenames) take `name` instead of tokenId — any REGISTERED name is biddable, listed or not. The agent reads its Seaport counter, signs, and POSTs the sign" → after: "Prepare a BID/offer on a position: returns the Seaport order to sign (EIP-712), the currency approval needed, and how to submit it. The agent reads its Seaport counter, signs, and POSTs the signed order — settlement stays on Seaport."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
